whatIs: Material Symbols is Google's icon collection, available in three styles and as a variable font with four adjustable axes: fill (FILL, from 0 to 1), weight (wght, from 100 to 700), grade (GRAD) and optical size (opsz, from 20 to 48 dp). This way a single icon can change weight or fill without loading different files.

Besides the web font, they can be downloaded as SVG and PNG, as Vector Drawable for Android and as Apple Symbols for iOS. It's a good fit when you want icons with a Material look and fine control over their style.
uses: Showing the active state of a button by transitioning FILL from 0 to 1.
Adjusting the icon weight to match the weight of your interface typography.
Reusing the same icons on web, Android and iOS by downloading each format.
caveats: The full variable font is heavy; restrict the axes and the icon list when requesting it from Google Fonts.

If you don't declare the axes in the Google Fonts URL, the font arrives with fixed values (weight 400, optical size 48, grade 0 and no fill) and you won't be able to change them with font-variation-settings.
If you use standalone SVGs you lose the variable axes: those adjustments are specific to the font.
idealFor: Interfaces that need Material icons with adjustable style.
